Can I Build Your Website in a Day? Yes. That's Not the Point.

By Marie Glow StudioPublished September 28, 2026

Yes, a website can be built in a day, and I have built websites very quickly myself. Speed just is not what I lead with. I would rather spend the first stretch getting to know your business, and a stopwatch skips that part.

I also have seven kids and a life, so no, I am not going to pretend every week looks the same. That is the joke. The real reason is about your website, not my calendar.

Can a website really be built in a day?

Technically, yes. A single page with a clear offer, finished copy, final photos and a logo can come together very fast. Some designers and agencies offer a website in a day or a week, and for the right client that model can work. If your branding, photos, words and decisions are all finished, fast is realistic.

Being found is a different clock. Google's documentation says crawling can take anywhere from a few days to a few weeks, and that requesting a crawl does not guarantee your page shows up in search results right away, or at all. So a site can be live in a day and still take a while to appear in search. Google explains the options, including its URL Inspection tool and sitemaps, in its guidance on asking for a recrawl.

Build time is not the same as project time

The build is where pages get put together, and it can be the quickest part of the job. A project is bigger. Depending on the business, it can also include:

  • Research and strategy
  • Copy and other content
  • Photos and assets
  • Search setup and on page SEO
  • Your feedback and revisions
  • Mobile testing and accessibility checks
  • Analytics, forms, booking links and other integrations
  • Final testing and launch preparation

Not every project needs every item, but skipping one does not make the work disappear. A page built in a day can look great and still say the wrong thing to the wrong person.

What do I want to know before I build anything?

I want time to understand your business before I build the thing that's supposed to represent it.

That means the basics first: what you sell, who your customer is and why they pick you over someone else. Then the questions customers keep asking, your business goals, and what you want a visitor to do, whether that is buy, book, call or ask for a quote. If there is an existing site, I want to know what is wrong with it. I also want your brand personality, what content the site needs, the search opportunities and any technical requirements.

Take three made up examples, not real clients. A baker's customers may want to see flavors and how to order, fast. A contractor's customers are probably comparing three quotes and need an easy way to ask for one. A stylist needs the booking link where a nervous new client will actually see it. Those differences shape the page far more than the build speed does.

How does discovery work for a one page site?

Every project starts with understanding the business. For the Website Starter, that happens through the intake, a short questionnaire covering your branding, photos, copy, contact information and social links. The page then follows a set shape: who you are, proof of your work, what you offer, and a clear way to reach you. The fixed shape is a big part of why it can move quickly.

So why don't you promise a fixed turnaround?

I do state timelines, and I stand behind them. What I don't do is make speed the headline. The Website Starter is guaranteed: five business days from a completed intake, or the revision round is free. I can promise that because the scope is fixed, with one page built from scratch around your brand colors, fonts, logo, photos and copy, plus basic on page SEO, domain connection help, basic pre launch testing and one revision round.

The Complete Website and Brand Identity package runs roughly two to three weeks, depending on how quickly your photos and content arrive. It includes a custom logo, brand colors, a style guide, social media graphics and a full multi page site, so there is more to decide along the way.

Either way, the schedule is only as quick as the material you bring. Someone who arrives with branding, photography, copy and offers settled is a different project from someone who needs help developing them. If the intake is not complete yet, the Starter's five days simply have not started.

What can fit in a day, and what needs more time?

Piece of the projectFits in a day?
Building a one page layoutYes, if the copy, photos and logo are finished
Writing copy and taking photosOnly if they already exist; the Starter includes neither
Your review and revisionsDepends on how fast you can look and reply
Google crawling the siteNo, Google says a few days to a few weeks, with no guarantee

Who is a fast website a good fit for?

Someone whose decisions are already made. Picture a spa owner with a finished logo, professional photos, a short service list and a booking link she already uses. She has served her customers for years, so a fixed scope and a fast timeline suit her well. Now picture a maker who is still choosing a name, has no photos and cannot decide between selling online and taking custom orders. Speed would only give her a faster version of an unfinished idea. Both are made up, and they are at different starting lines.

What should I have ready before a website project starts?

For the Website Starter, the intake asks for your logo, brand colors and fonts if you have them, business information, photos, copy, contact details, social links and your call to action. Copywriting and custom photography are not part of the Starter, so those need to exist first. Having everything ready is the biggest thing you control about how fast any website goes, mine or anyone else's.

If you run a service business, decide which action you want first: a booking link, a quote form or a phone call. What a service business website needs walks through that choice, and how long it takes to build a website covers the timeline for each type of build.

Is a faster website a better website?

Not by itself. I don't want your website finished as fast as possible. I want it finished as well as possible without dragging the project out unnecessarily. Sometimes that is five business days. If something important is missing from the intake, the honest move is to finish gathering it first, not to rush past it.

AI can speed up parts of the work, and I use it myself. Whether to build a site with it on your own is a separate question, and I take it on in can AI build a website. If you have a hard date, such as an event or a launch, tell me on the contact page and I will say honestly whether it is realistic.

If your branding, photos and words are ready and you want a professional page live quickly, the Website Starter is built for that. If you need the brand and a full site together, look at the Complete package, or see all services to compare.

Frequently asked questions

Can a website be built in a day?

Yes, a small one page website can be built in a day when the copy, photos, logo and decisions are already finished. Build time is only part of a project, though. Discovery, revisions, testing and launch preparation take extra time, and Google says crawling can take a few days to a few weeks, so being found in search runs on its own timeline.

How long does the Website Starter take?

Five business days, counted from the point your intake is complete, and it is guaranteed: if it runs over, the revision round costs you nothing. Having your logo, photos, copy and contact details ready is what keeps it that fast.

Why does the Complete Website package take two to three weeks?

It includes more work: a custom logo, brand colors, a style guide, social media graphics and a full multi page site. It takes roughly two to three weeks depending on how quickly your photos and content arrive.

What do I need ready before starting a website?

For the Website Starter: your logo, brand colors and fonts if you have them, business information, photos, copy, contact details, social links and your call to action. Copywriting and custom photography are not included, so those need to exist first.
